summary: Database unreachable, wrong DB credentials and query timeouts were answered 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and sent to Sentry per request. My first fix (from a raw-query probe, code P2010) was insufficient: real pg-adapter errors carry the errno as the Prisma error code (ECONNREFUSED) and transactions raise AggregateError.
evidence: End-to-end run with Postgres stopped: 500 on every DB request (first build); 503 after the fix; recovery 200 on restart
recommended_fix: Map network errno codes, Prisma availability codes, PG classes 08/28/53/57P01-03, init errors and exact pg driver messages to 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE as a handled warning; unknown errors stay 500
regression_test: all-exceptions.filter.spec.ts (25 tests); failure.mjs run; security.api + qa.adversarial

evidence: End-to-end run with Redis stopped: 500 first build; 503 after the fix; recovery 200

summary: Negative numbers were exported as text with a leading apostrophe because the formula guard also prefixed numbers.

component: health.controller.ts (readiness uses the shared DB pool, 2 s timeout); render.yaml healthCheckPath=/health/ready; DATABASE_POOL_MAX default 10
class: probable defect (observed locally, not reproduced on Render)
summary: Under 100 concurrent clients on one Node process the readiness probe returned 503 twice in 49 calls because its SELECT 1 waited for a pool connection longer than 2 s. Render uses this endpoint as the health check, so load can make an instance look unhealthy and amplify the overload.
evidence: scripts/load run, concurrency 100: health 2/49 503; ALL p95 7108 ms
recommended_fix: Use a dedicated single connection (or a separate tiny pool) for readiness, or treat pool-wait timeouts as busy-not-down; review DATABASE_POOL_MAX against the Supabase pooler limit
regression_test: load test at concurrency above pool size asserting ready stays 200
